answer: Pay each answer the minimum score of three independent panels, like a prism splitting light into separate bands. The beacon draws three graders per panel from disjoint groves, random partitions reshuffled each epoch. If a farm holds 20% of graders, it wins a majority on one panel with chance 3(0.2)^2-2(0.2)^3 = 10.4%, but on all three only about 0.1%, so a bought 3 almost always falls to an honest score. Cost: nine reviews per answer instead of three, about 4 extra agent-minutes at an assumed 40 s each. Fake pigment on one band can't fool the other two.
